judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same BASIC 6 coordinate (rank 2) in Strand 1: Number. Nomination signals (shared Strand/Grade ancestors, weak rank proximity, weak 'b5/3' code-prefix overlap, low Jaccard token overlap driven mainly by 'angles') are examination triggers only; the decision rests on the shared angle-property content. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so absence of stronger sequencing evidence in this bounded excerpt is not proof of absence.

Same-rank direction rests on substantive skill content, not code order: B6.2.1.1.7 and its Learning Components require expressing a given pattern's rule in words and then in algebra, i.e. producing a symbolic generalisation of a pattern; B6.2.1.1.8 requires describing the relationship embedded in a given table or chart using a mathematical expression, which applies that same symbolisation skill to a data-representation context where the pattern must first be extracted from tabular/graphical form. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2, identical grade coordinate) under the same Content Standard B6.1.1.1 on quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals, within Strand 1 Number / Sub-Strand 1 Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality. B6.1.1.1.6 asks learners to skip count forwards and backwards in 5000s/10,000s up to and from 1,000,000, while B6.1.1.1.2 asks them to read and write numbers in figures and in words up to 1,000,000,000 (LCs: read/write numbers in figures and words vs. skip count forwards/backwards). These are complementary large-number skills — numerical sequencing versus symbolic and verbal representation — that reinforce the same place-value understanding, but the bounded evidence does not show one being substantively deeper or an extension of the other, and same-rank placement provides no developmental direction. The shared code prefix, shared ancestors, and generic token overlap ('000', '1', 'up', 'to') are nomination signals only, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same canonical coordinate rank 2) under Strand 1: Number, but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.3.1.3 (Fractions) asks learners to use models to explain multiplying a fraction by a whole number, a whole number by a fraction, and a fraction by a fraction, while B6.1.2.1.1 (Number Operations) asks learners to apply mental strategies and number properties (skip counting, doubling/halving, 9s/11s patterns) to determine basic multiplication facts to 81 and related division facts. Their Learning Components confirm distinct targets: fraction-multiplication modelling versus mental recall of basic multiplication/division facts. The coherence is substantive — both develop understanding of multiplication as an operation within the same grade's Number strand, and fact fluency reinforces computation in fraction work — but the fraction indicator's demand is conceptual model-based explanation rather than fact recall, and at equal rank there is no substantive evidence that proficiency in one specifically supports success in the other, so a developmental direction is not justified. Shared ancestors (Grade, Strand), code prefix 'b6.1', and the single shared LC tag 'multiplication' are weak nomination signals, not dependency evidence.
